entities.name: King Sejong the Great
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
The fourth king of the Joseon dynasty (r. 1418–1450 CE) and the most revered monarch in Korean history. Sejong's reign is considered the golden age of Korean civilization: he commissioned the creation of the Korean alphabet (Hangul, 1443–1446 CE), one of the most scientifically designed writing systems in history; established the Jiphyeonjeon (Hall of Worthies) — a royal academy of scholars; promoted advances in astronomy (rain gauge, sundials, celestial globes), agriculture, printing technology, and music; and expanded Korean territory.

His creation of Hangul — expressly to promote literacy among common people who could not master Chinese characters — is one of the noblest acts of statesmanship in world history. He appears on the Korean 10,000-won banknote and his statue dominates Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: King Sejong's creation of Hangul led to a significant increase in literacy among common people, promoting education and cultural development. By 1500 CE, literacy rates had improved from 1% to 30%, contributing to the growth of a more educated and informed population.
